title: My first month in Edinburgh
text:
Dear Aunt Basia,

I'm sorry I haven't written sooner, but my first month in Edinburgh has been incredibly busy! I've finally unpacked all my boxes, and my little room in the student residence is starting to feel like home.

The university is amazing. The buildings are old and beautiful, and some of the lecture halls are so big that I sometimes get lost on my way to class. My course is harder than I expected, especially statistics, but my tutor, Dr Campbell, is very patient and always answers my questions after the lectures.

I share a kitchen with five other students – two from Scotland, one from Italy, one from India and one from Canada. We take turns cooking dinner on Sundays, so I've already learnt to make a real curry! Last week I made pierogi for everyone. They weren't perfect, but they disappeared in ten minutes.

The only thing I'm still not used to is the weather. It changes every hour – sun, rain, wind and sun again. Everybody here says you should never leave home without a raincoat, and they're right.

To earn some extra money, I've started working in a café near the castle on Saturday mornings. The pay isn't great, but my English is improving fast because I talk to customers all the time.

I'm coming home for Christmas on 20th December. Mum says you're going to make your famous poppy seed cake – please save a big piece for me!

Lots of love,
Zosia
